facts.raw_span: A woman in her 60s with a history of hypertension
sudden-onset chest pain
no history of any acute febrile illness
no family history of sudden cardiac death
tachycardic with a pulse of 120 beats/min
blood pressure was normal
White blood cell count: 14,300/µL
Serum calcium: within normal limits
High-sensitivity troponin I: 1.15 ng/mL
Brain-type natriuretic peptide: 1060.30 pg/mL
Initial ECG showed sinus tachycardia, PR-segment elevation in lead aVR, PR-segment depression in leads I, II, III, aVF, and V4 to V6
Contrast-enhanced abdominal CT: revealed an enhanced left-adrenal heterogeneous mass measuring 4.1 × 3.4 cm

Brain-type natriuretic peptide: 1060.30 pg/mL
Initial ECG showed sinus tachycardia, PR-segment elevation in lead aVR, PR-segment depression in leads I, II, III, aVF, and V4 to V6
Contrast-enhanced abdominal CT: revealed an enhanced left-adrenal heterogeneous mass measuring 4.1 × 3.4 cm

concepts.why: The patient presented with sudden-onset chest pain, elevated troponin, and characteristic ECG changes, which are consistent with Takotsubo cardiomyopathy.
The patient has an enhanced left-adrenal heterogeneous mass, which is suggestive of pheochromocytoma.
The patient presented with chest pain and elevated troponin, which are consistent with myocardial infarction, although the coronary angiography showed normal coronary arteries.
The patient has an elevated white blood cell count, which is suggestive of sepsis, although there is no clear source of infection.

rationales.F02: Chest pain is a common symptom of myocardial infarction and Takotsubo cardiomyopathy.
rationales.F05: Tachycardia can be seen in various conditions including myocardial infarction, Takotsubo cardiomyopathy, and pheochromocytoma.
rationales.F09: Elevated troponin levels are indicative of myocardial infarction and can also be seen in Takotsubo cardiomyopathy.
rationales.F10: Elevated brain-type natriuretic peptide levels are often seen in heart failure, which can be a complication of myocardial infarction and Takotsubo cardiomyopathy.
rationales.F11: The described ECG changes are consistent with myocardial infarction and Takotsubo cardiomyopathy.
rationales.F12: The presence of an adrenal mass is highly suggestive of pheochromocytoma.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's presentation with sudden-onset chest pain, elevated troponin and BNP levels, and the ECG findings are consistent with Takotsubo cardiomyopathy, which is further supported by the left ventriculography showing systolic apical ballooning.
